overall: As of ~01:45 ET (10:45 PM PT), Los Angeles is sitting at 68°F with zero warming velocity — essentially at its overnight low. Despite active Heat Advisories and an Extreme Heat Warning covering broader Southern California (beaches low 80s, inland near 90s), the immediate LA coastal/urban area is tracking notably cooler, reflecting the typical marine-layer moderation that keeps the coast insulated from inland heat events. No meaningful temperature rise is underway.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show meaningful spread: HRRR and NBM cluster tightly at 73.5–73.6°F, ECMWF sits at 75.6°F, and GFS is an outlier at 78.2°F. The high-resolution, short-range HRRR is best suited to capture local coastal dynamics here and aligns closely with NBM, suggesting GFS is running warm; the NWS official Tuesday forecast of 76°F splits the difference but likely skews slightly high relative to where current models are converging.
max_temp_prediction: The weight of evidence — HRRR and NBM both at ~73.5°F, ECMWF at 75.6°F, and the D1_NOW model assigning 58.7% probability to the 72–73°F even bucket — points to a today's high in the 73–74°F range. The active Kalshi even-bucket market (72–73°F top bucket) is well-supported by the two most reliable short-range models. Confidence is moderately high; the main upside risk is if the GFS and NWS official 76°F scenario verify, but marine influence and model consensus argue against it.
